title: What is an algorithm?
examples: Can you give me an example of an algorithm for brushing teeth?
What is the difference between a list of steps and a real algorithm?
If I change one step, does the whole algorithm break?

explain.say: An algorithm is just a set of clear instructions to solve a problem.

draw.text: Algorithm: Clear steps to solve a problem

explain.say: These instructions must always be in the correct order to work right.

items: Start: Need to bake a cake

explain.say: Sorting means putting things into a specific, organized order.
Efficiency means finding the fastest way to follow those instructions.
For example, finding the biggest number in a group is a simple algorithm.

items: 1 | Look at the first number | Current Max: 10
2 | Compare to the next number | Current Max: 15

explain.say: In real life, following recipe steps is like using an algorithm.

faq.q: What is the difference between an algorithm and a recipe?
faq.a: A recipe is a type of algorithm, but an algorithm can solve any problem, not just cooking.
asks: Can algorithms be used for non-cooking things?

faq.q: If I skip a step, what happens to my algorithm?
faq.a: Skipping a step usually means the output will be wrong or the process will fail completely.
asks: What if I mix up the instructions?

faq.q: What does 'efficiency' mean when talking about algorithms?
faq.a: Efficiency means doing the job using the fewest steps or the least amount of time possible.
asks: How do I make an algorithm more efficient?

faq.q: Do I have to use code to make an algorithm?
faq.a: No, you can write an algorithm using simple words and steps before you write any code.
asks: Can I plan it on paper?
Is pseudocode the same as an algorithm?

faq.q: What is sorting in the context of coding?
faq.a: Sorting is the process of arranging a list of items, like numbers or names, into a specific order, usually ascending or descending.
asks: How do I put these numbers in order?
Is sorting always done from smallest to largest?

facts: An algorithm must have a clear start and a definite end.
The steps must be unambiguous so everyone follows them the same way.
Sorting arranges data into a specific sequence, like alphabetical or numerical order.
Efficiency measures how quickly and with how few resources a task can be completed.

quiz.say: To find the largest number in the list 12, 5, 20, what is the first step?

options.show: Compare the first two numbers to find a temporary maximum.
options.say: Compare the first two numbers to find a temporary maximum.

options.show: Just pick the biggest number you see.
options.say: Just pick the biggest number you see.

quiz.why: You must start somewhere, so comparing the first two gives you a starting point.

wrong.0: Sorting is a whole process, not just the first step.
wrong.1: This changes the numbers and does not help find the largest.
wrong.3: This is guessing, not following a set process.

quiz.say: If you have the numbers 10, 30, 20 and you sort them, what is the correct order?
quiz.why: Sorting means putting them in order, from smallest to largest in this case.

wrong.0: This order is mixed up and does not follow any clear rule.
wrong.2: This is sorting in descending order, but the question implies standard order.
wrong.3: This is the original, unsorted order.

quiz.say: Which of these methods is the most efficient way to check if a word is spelled correctly?

options.show: Comparing the word to a known dictionary list.
options.say: Comparing the word to a known dictionary list.

options.show: Asking three different people to check.
options.say: Asking three different people to check.

quiz.why: Checking against a known list is fast because you only need to match it to one place.

wrong.0: Writing it repeatedly does not prove it is spelled correctly.
wrong.2: This takes too much time and is not reliable.
wrong.3: This involves too many people and is not a systematic process.
